text.p: An outbreak of gastroenteritis in a remote district of western Nepal has killed 19 people in a month and a half, health officials said on Friday.
They said 80 people in five villages of Jumla district had contracted the disease caused by contaminated food and water. The government has sent a medical team to the area.

"The problem is that we get information about the outbreak of the disease only after the patients die," said Beni Bahadur Karki, director of the epidemiology and disease control division at the Health Ministry.
He said poverty and a lack of awareness about basic hygiene were the main causes of the fatalities.
Mountainous Nepal is one of the 10 poorest countries in the world and most of its villages are located in the remote foothills of the Himalayas. Infrastructure including communication is poor.
Last month 25 people were killed in central Nepal by cholera and 85 people died in an outbreak of measles in the western part of the kingdom.
